title: Prior research
summary: User's full 279-line note read. Pure-bridge elimination and triple-component completion are promising restricted algorithms; all new claims await independent checks and Lean proofs.

claims.label: Pure-bridge elimination
claims.detail: The note proposes deepest-root elimination with degree-two marks and a one-cut exchange. Marked local queries are paid for by role-swapping to a tree–forest problem. Verify geometry, exchange, and q_J≤d_D independently.

claims.label: Triple completion DP
claims.detail: The note proposes O(nm) value computation when every incompatible source component has exactly three leaves. Independently establish the characterization, DP invariant and witness reconstruction.

claims.label: Reported test counts
claims.detail: The note describes extensive tests, but its implementation bundle was not supplied. These reported counts are not reproduced campaign evidence.

claims.label: Balanced safe cover
claims.detail: The note explicitly leaves optimum-preserving construction of at most O*(1.25^b) terminal refinements with local distance≤b/2 unproved. Arbitrary pre-cutting can exclude every optimum.

lemmas.label: Pure-overlap clearance
lemmas.detail: A block using one vertex of a pure degree-two overlap must use its entire path. Verify all root and single-vertex cases.

lemmas.label: Marked elimination
lemmas.detail: Prove exact elimination and preservation of earlier marks, including many overlapping components.

lemmas.label: Pay for marked queries
lemmas.detail: Prove role-swap feasible-partition equality and residual cut budget q_J=h_D(J)-(r-1)≤d_D.

lemmas.label: Triple terminal solver
lemmas.detail: Prove the connected-region characterization and O(nm) DP with explicit reconstruction costs.

lemmas.label: Safe terminal cover
lemmas.detail: Generate a small terminal family retaining an original optimum; prove the size and balanced local-distance bound. This is the missing unrestricted improvement.

next: First independently test and formalize the two restricted terminal algorithms; then attack optimum-preserving safe covers of actual baseline hard children. Reconcile the prior 2^k thesis claim before novelty assertions.
